titleEn: Poly-B Pipe Replacement in Vancouver 2026: Insurance Deadlines, Strata Levies and What Homeowners Pay
titleZh: 温哥华 Poly-B 管道更换指南 2026：保险截止日期、共管公寓特别评估与业主费用详解
excerptEn: Poly-B pipes are failing across Metro Vancouver. Home insurers are non-renewing policies. Strata corporations are passing special levies. Here is what Vancouver homeowners pay for Poly-B replacement in 2026 and how the process works.
excerptZh: Poly-B 管道在温哥华地区全面老化失效。家庭保险续保被拒，共管公寓开始通过特别评估。2026 年温哥华业主更换 Poly-B 的费用是多少？流程是怎样的？本指南一一解答。
contentEn:
Poly-B pipe failure is no longer a hypothetical for Metro Vancouver homeowners — it is an active insurance crisis. Major Canadian home insurers have begun non-renewing policies on properties with Poly-B (polybutylene) plumbing, and strata corporations across Metro Vancouver are passing special levies to fund building-wide replacements. If you own a home or condo unit built between 1985 and 1999 in Richmond, Vancouver, Burnaby, Coquitlam or any other Metro Vancouver city, your property likely has Poly-B pipes and your insurer may already be watching the calendar.

Reno Stars has completed Poly-B to PEX replacement projects throughout Richmond, Vancouver and Burnaby. This guide covers what Poly-B is, why insurers are acting now, how the BC strata legal framework applies, what the replacement process involves, and what Vancouver homeowners actually paid in 2025–2026.

What Is Poly-B Pipe and Why Is It Failing?

Polybutylene (Poly-B) is a plastic plumbing pipe used in millions of Canadian homes built between approximately 1985 and 1999. It was marketed as a cost-effective alternative to copper and installed widely in new construction across Canada during that period. The pipe itself is gray or beige in colour and typically marked with "PB-2110" or similar markings.

Poly-B fails through a process called oxidation. The chlorine and other chemicals used in municipal water treatment interact with the pipe's internal material, causing it to become brittle and prone to micro-cracking over time. The pipe's fittings — often made of brass or acetal plastic — are the most common failure point, though the pipe itself can also split or rupture without warning. Failures are not always gradual; a pipe that appears fine on inspection can fail catastrophically overnight.

What Does Insurance Non-Renewal Mean for Vancouver Homeowners?

Starting around 2022, several major Canadian insurance providers began declining to renew home insurance policies on properties confirmed to have Poly-B plumbing. This is not universal — some insurers will still cover Poly-B homes with a documented inspection, a signed plumber's declaration, or a recent re-pipe — but the trend is toward restriction, not expansion of coverage.

The practical consequence for a Metro Vancouver homeowner is this: if your insurer does not renew your policy, you must find alternative coverage. In British Columbia, homeowners without valid home insurance cannot obtain a mortgage through most federally regulated lenders. A non-renewal notice from your insurer is therefore not merely an administrative inconvenience — it can trigger a financial emergency if not addressed promptly.

How BC Strata Law Drives Building-Wide Poly-B Replacement

Under the BC Strata Property Act, a strata corporation may raise a special levy to fund major capital repairs or replacements that affect the common property or common assets. Poly-B replacement in a building's common supply lines qualifies as such a repair in most interpretations.

What this means in practice: if your building's main supply lines are Poly-B, the strata corporation can pass a special levy — sometimes exceeding $10,000 to $25,000 per unit — and assess that levy against all unit owners whether or not an individual unit's interior plumbing has failed. Individual unit owners cannot opt out, and the strata corporation may place a lien on a unit if the levy is not paid.

Coordinated, building-wide Poly-B replacement offers a material cost advantage. When a single contractor can schedule work across multiple units in a building, rather than dispatching crews repeatedly, the per-unit cost is typically 15% to 25% lower than isolated individual replacements. Reno Stars works directly with strata councils to design building-wide replacement schedules that minimize disruption and reduce per-unit cost through coordinated scheduling.

Poly-B Replacement Process: What Homeowners Experience

Poly-B replacement involves routing new PEX (cross-linked polyethylene) supply lines from the building's main manifold or water meter to every fixture in the home — sinks, toilets, showers, baths, washing machine connections and any other hot or cold water outlet.

The typical project scope includes: shutting off the building or unit's water supply; removing accessible Poly-B pipe sections; installing new PEX lines following the existing routing where possible; replacing all shutoff valves at each fixture; pressure-testing the new system to confirm no leaks; and patching and refinishing drywall at access points.

PEX is the current standard for residential plumbing in Canada. It carries a 50-year manufacturer warranty from major producers, is resistant to chlorine corrosion, and does not suffer from the oxidation issues that affect Poly-B. PEX is flexible, meaning it can be routed around obstacles with fewer fittings than rigid copper — which reduces the number of potential leak points.

Most residential Poly-B replacement projects in Metro Vancouver take between three and seven working days for a standard single-family home, and one to three days per condo unit in a coordinated building project.

Poly-B Replacement Cost Vancouver 2025–2026

Actual project costs from Reno Stars' completed work in Metro Vancouver provide the most reliable benchmark:

  • Condo unit (Richmond, 800–1,100 sq ft interior): $3,200–$5,500 including shutoff valves and drywall patch
  • Single-family home (Vancouver, 1,800–2,400 sq ft): $6,500–$11,000 including full supply-line replacement and pressure test
  • Strata building coordination (per unit, 15–25% discount applied): $2,700–$4,600 for comparable scope in Richmond buildings
  • Additional: exterior underground service line replacement: $1,800–$3,500

These figures are from Reno Stars' actual invoices. Your property may fall outside this range depending on site-specific conditions identified during the pre-project inspection.

Do I Have to Replace Poly-B Right Now?

There is no BC provincial mandate requiring individual homeowners to replace Poly-B pipes by a fixed date. However, the practical and financial consequences of delay are real and compounding: insurers are actively restricting coverage; if your building's strata has passed a special levy, your share is due regardless of individual replacement status; Poly-B failures can occur with little or no warning; and if you sell, a home inspector will note the presence of Poly-B on the condition report, and buyers increasingly use that to negotiate price reductions or require replacement as a condition of sale.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does BC home insurance cover Poly-B pipe failure?

Coverage depends on your insurer and policy. Some insurers will cover a sudden Poly-B pipe burst under standard home insurance, but many are now declining to renew policies on properties with confirmed Poly-B plumbing. Once your insurer non-renews, finding replacement coverage requires either a licensed plumber's inspection report confirming the pipe condition, proof of completed replacement with PEX, or acceptance of a policy with a Poly-B exclusion. A non-renewal is not the same as cancellation — act immediately on a non-renewal notice, before the renewal deadline passes.

Can I sell my Vancouver home with Poly-B pipes?

You can, but the sale process is materially more complex. BC home inspectors include plumbing material in their standard condition report, and buyers' agents are increasingly aware of Poly-B insurance issues. A buyer who cannot obtain insurance — or who must pay a higher premium because of the Poly-B disclosure — will typically negotiate a price reduction or require replacement as a condition of sale. Replacing before listing typically yields a cleaner transaction and a higher sale price than replacing as a sale condition.

What is the lifespan of Poly-B pipe?

Poly-B was originally rated for 25–30 years of service life under ideal conditions. Most Poly-B installed in Metro Vancouver between 1985 and 1999 is now 27 to 41 years old, exceeding the original service life rating. Oxidation and brittleness have accelerated in many installations, particularly in buildings with aggressive municipal water treatment. There is no reliable way to predict when a specific pipe will fail — the only definitive preventive measure is replacement with PEX.

Is PEX plumbing code-approved in British Columbia?

Yes. PEX (cross-linked polyethylene) is approved for use in residential plumbing systems under the British Columbia Building Code and by all major Canadian plumbing code authorities. It is the standard material used in new residential construction in Canada today. A licensed plumber using code-compliant PEX installation methods is fully compliant with BC requirements.

How long does a Poly-B to PEX replacement take?

For a standard Vancouver single-family home, the active replacement work typically takes three to seven working days. For an individual condo unit in a coordinated building project, one to three days is typical. The timeline depends on the size of the property, the number of fixtures, and whether drywall must be opened at access points. Reno Stars provides a project-specific timeline as part of the pre-project inspection and quote process.

contentZh:
Poly-B 管道老化失效已不再是温哥华业主的假设风险，而是正在发生的保险危机。加拿大主要家庭保险提供商已开始拒绝为装有 Poly-B（聚丁烯）管道的房产续保，而大温哥华地区的共管公寓 corporation 正在通过特别评估为全楼管道更换筹集资金。

如果您在大温哥华的列治文、温哥华、本拿比、高贵林或任何其他城市拥有 1985 年至 1999 年间建成的房屋或公寓，您的房产很可能装有 Poly-B 管道，而您的保险公司可能已经在关注截止日期。

什么是 Poly-B 管道？为何会失效？

聚丁烯（Poly-B）是一种塑料水管，应用于约 1985 年至 1999 年间建造的数百万加拿大住宅。管道通常呈灰色或米色，并标有 "PB-2110" 或类似标记。

Poly-B 通过氧化过程失效。自来水处理中使用的氯和其他化学物质与管道内部材料发生反应，导致其变脆并容易产生微裂纹。管道的管件通常由黄铜或缩醛塑料制成，是最常见的故障点，但管道本身也可能在无预警的情况下破裂或断裂。

保险拒绝续保对温哥华业主意味着什么？

大约从 2022 年开始，几家大型加拿大保险提供商开始拒绝为已确认装有 Poly-B 管道的房产续保。这并非普遍现象——部分保险公司仍会承保带有 Poly-B 的房屋，但需要提供经记录的检查报告、持牌水管工的声明或最近的管道更换证明。但趋势是限制而非放宽。

对于大温哥华业主来说，如果您的保险公司不续保，您必须寻找替代保险。在 BC 省，没有有效房屋保险的业主无法通过大多数联邦监管贷款机构获得抵押贷款。因此，保险公司拒绝续保通知不仅仅是行政上的不便——如果不及时处理，还可能引发财务危机。

BC 省共管公寓法律如何推动全楼 Poly-B 更换

根据 BC 省《共管公寓法》，共管公寓 corporation 可以征收特别评估以资助影响公共财产或公共资产的主要资本维修或更换。全楼 Poly-B 更换在大多数解释下都符合此类维修资格。

如果您的楼宇主管是 Poly-B，共管公寓 corporation 可以通过特别评估——有时每单元超过 10,000 至 25,000 加元——并向所有单元业主分摊费用。个别业主不能选择退出，如果未缴纳评估费用，共管公寓 corporation 可能会对单元设置留置权。

协调的全楼 Poly-B 更换具有实质性成本优势。当单个承包商可以在大楼内多个单元安排工作时，相比零散的单独更换，每单元成本通常降低 15% 至 25%。Reno Stars 直接与共管公寓 council 合作，设计全楼更换时间表，以减少干扰并降低每单元成本。

Poly-B 更换流程：业主的经历

Poly-B 更换涉及从大楼主歧管或水表到房屋每个装置铺设新的 PEX（交联聚乙烯）管道。

典型工程范围包括：关闭大楼或单元的供水；拆除可触及的 Poly-B 管段；在现有布线可行的情况下沿现有路线安装新 PEX 管道；更换每个装置的所有截止阀；对新系统进行压力测试以确认无泄漏；以及修补和整理接入点的干墙。

PEX 是加拿大住宅管道当前的行业标准。它享有主要制造商 50 年产品质保，耐氯腐蚀，且不受影响 Poly-B 的氧化问题困扰。PEX 具有柔性，意味着可以用更少的管件绕过障碍物——减少了潜在的泄漏点。

Poly-B 更换费用 2025–2026

来自 Reno Stars 已完成大温哥华地区项目的实际工程成本提供了最可靠的基准：

  • 公寓单元（列治文，800–1,100 平方英尺室内面积）：$3,200–$5,500，含截止阀和干墙修补
  • 独立住宅（温哥华，1,800–2,400 平方英尺）：$6,500–$11,000，含全供水管更换和压力测试
  • 共管公寓协调（每单元，适用 15–25% 折扣）：列治文大楼同类工程 $2,700–$4,600
  • 附加：外部地下服务管更换：$1,800–$3,500

常见问题

BC 房屋保险是否承保 Poly-B 管道故障？

coverage取决于您的保险公司和保单。部分保险公司会通过标准房屋保险承保突发 Poly-B 管道爆裂，但许多公司现在拒绝为已确认 Poly-B 管道的房产续保。一旦您的保险公司拒绝续保，寻找替代保险需要提供持牌水管工的检查报告、PEX 更换完成的证明，或接受带有 Poly-B 排除条款的保单。拒绝续保不等于取消——请在续保截止日期前立即采取行动。

Poly-B 管道寿命有多长？

Poly-B 最初在理想条件下额定使用寿命为 25-30 年。1985 年至 1999 年间安装在大温哥华的绝大多数 Poly-B 管道目前已有 27 至 41 年，超过原始使用寿命额定值。氧化和脆化已经加速。没有可靠的方法来预测特定管道何时会发生故障——唯一明确的预防措施是用 PEX 更换。

PEX 管道在 BC 省是否获准使用？

是的。PEX（交联聚乙烯）已获准在加拿大住宅管道系统中使用，符合 BC 省建筑规范和所有主要加拿大管道规范当局的要求。使用符合规范的 PEX 安装方法的持牌水管工完全符合 BC 省要求。

Poly-B 更换需要多长时间？

对于温哥华标准独立住宅，主动更换工程通常需要三到七个工作日。对于协调建筑项目中的单个公寓单元，通常为一到三天。实际时间取决于房产大小、装置数量以及是否需要打开干墙接入点。Reno Stars 在项目前检查和报价流程中提供特定项目的时间表。
